name: gizza-ai/chorus
summary: Add a configurable chorus effect to an audio file

tool.description: Add a chorus effect to an audio file by mixing in short modulated delay voices with ffmpeg. Provide either url (HTTP/HTTPS) or ref (id from a prior tool call). voices controls how many delayed copies are mixed (2-4); delay_ms is the base delay; depth_ms and speed_hz control the modulation; decay is the delayed voice level. Output is re-encoded to mp3, wav, ogg, flac, or m4a and embedded album art is dropped. Runs locally through the ffmpeg runtime.

decay.description: Level of each delayed voice (0.1-0.9, default 0.4). Higher values make the chorus wetter and louder.

delay_ms.description: Base delay before the first chorus voice, in milliseconds (20-80, default 50). Later voices are staggered by 8 ms.

depth_ms.description: Modulation depth in milliseconds (1-8, default 2). Higher values make the pitch movement more obvious.

format.description: Output audio format. Default mp3 (192 kbps); wav/flac are lossless re-encodes, ogg is Vorbis, m4a is AAC.

ref.description: Reference id from a prior tool call. Use either url or ref.

speed_hz.description: Modulation rate in Hertz (0.1-5, default 0.4). Higher values shimmer or wobble faster.

url.description: Audio URL (HTTP/HTTPS). Use either url or ref.

voices.description: Number of delayed modulation voices to mix in (2-4, default 2). More voices sound wider and thicker.
